pensamiento:
I'm checking each user story against the quality criteria one by one. The first four look fine: role and action are there, the objective is a single feature, there are no notes, and the benefit is a real purpose. I'm now looking at QUS-005, where the "Hidden state" wording seems to be a feature that's acceptable.

Next I'm running through QUS-006 to QUS-009 against the same criteria. The "discoverable via OpenSpending" wording and the vague benefit phrasing look acceptable, since the owner and admins still have access and "Hidden" is clear enough. I'm checking for conflicts with CTX-OS-087 and seeing none, since that one hides a public dataset while this one adds a new hidden dataset. Then I'm looking at the uniqueness and formatting of QUS-008 and QUS-009, and noting that the empty title isn't part of the criteria.

I'm settling on INV-003 as estimable: the criteria define the hidden behaviour, though "embeddable visualisations" and what counts as the owner are still a bit unclear. For INV-004 I'm leaning toward an estimate of 5 rather than 3, since the visibility filter has to cross search, listings, embeds and admin access.

I'm checking the remaining items against the criteria. INV-005 looks observable: the Public/Hidden choice, the exclusion from search, listings and embeds, and the immediate searchability all can be verified, though "immediately" is a little loose. For DOR-001, the search, listing and embed parts are all within the same platform, so I don't see an outside dependency yet.

I'm settling on an estimate of 5 for the story rather than 3, since the visibility filter has to reach search, listings, embeds and the owner's view, and the change to Public has to work too. The business rules for default, visibility and access are all explicit, so I'm not seeing a need for further error-case criteria. The non-functional side doesn't look critical for this kind of feature. The empty title isn't part of the catalog criteria, so I'll leave it alone. I don't see any instructions embedded in the stories, so all the criteria pass and I'm accepting the set.

Now I'm drafting the refined story in Spanish and starting on the acceptance criteria, which I'm translating into Spanish as I go.

I'm writing out the acceptance criteria in Spanish now, covering the owner's and admins' access to hidden datasets and the switch from Hidden to Public, then settling on the functional type and an estimate of 5.
